summary: Config-only, shape-disjoint re-run of a kernel already measured three times on the dense-chain base (sliding decode_16 +3.8% isolated, +5.5% and +5.2% in the two stacks), now limited to 2 <= batch <= 16; sliding decode_16 is the only shape that changes and the other 11 shapes are in-run controls, so no companion is needed. Two build points must be fixed in the change text: keep S=16 (master's _num_splits would give 4 at B=16) and do not paste the patch's helper hunk, which would duplicate master's helpers.
justification: Plausible and already shown. At sliding decode_16, master still runs SGLang's chain between the qkv GEMM and the o GEMM: FusedQKNorm+RoPE, k/v FP8 casts, store_cache, q cast, FA3 prepare + main (~13.6 us) + FlashAttnFwdCombine (~3.7 us), then FusedRMSNormGate. None of the landed hypotheses touched that chain. sliding-decode1 only gates batch 1, splitkv only gates window == 0, and the dense chain starts after the o GEMM. The same _sliding_fused_kernel (master's copy is byte-identical to the patch's helpers; I diffed them) moved sliding decode_16 217.1 -> 209.1 us (paired ratio 1.038) alone in b01fd2df. On the same dense-chain base it moved it 217.1 -> 195.4 (1.055) in 2193fc0d and 217.1 -> 190.5 (1.052) in b94e7973. That is three readings of 3.8-5.5%, all above the 1.5% per-shape noise. Expected directions match the gate. Batch 1 is master's _sliding_forward, full layers are splitkv/paired FA3, verify is q_len 8, and decode_32 is batch 32 > 16, so every one of those is a byte-identical control. Floors: sliding decode_16 is at 205.0 us against a 76.7 us floor; FA3 is not in its top three (Marlin 97.0, nvjet 26.3, P kernel 25.1), and the ~25-28 us attention chain is the part being cut. Headline impact is small. Sliding decode_16 at -8..-11 us x weight 46 saves ~370-500 us of a ~14.7 ms decode_16 load (~2.5-3.4%), about +0.4-0.6% on the 6-load geomean, well inside the ±1.5% CI. Judge it per shape: the kill rule is z>=2 on decode_16, and this cannot become a promotion on the headline by itself. Weakest link: the number of splits. The measured gain used S=16 hard-coded (512 CTAs at B=16, ~2 MB fp32 workspace). Master's _sliding_forward calls _num_splits(), which returns 4 at B=16. An implementer who widens master's batch-1 gate and reuses _sliding_forward will silently run S=4, a configuration that has never been measured inside the layer, and the result then attributes to the split count, not to the port. Second weakest: the parenthetical '(sliding decode_16 and the batch-8/9 tests)' is wrong. The batch-8 test (ctx 2047) uses the default page 64 (reference.py PAGE = 64), so the page==1 gate sends it to FA3. Only the batch-9 test (page 1, mixed spread) exercises the new path before timing. That is still adequate, because the batch-9 test passed in all three earlier runs.
confounders: full-decode-splitkv-restack-on-pdl (just landed, b047510): no mechanistic confound. Its gate is window == 0 and the new gate is window != 0, so sliding decode_16 never reaches it. Two mechanical caveats only: (1) kernel_fn now nests the splitkv/paired branch inside master's else, so the patch's kernel_fn hunk (base 90040c7) will not apply and must be hand-merged; (2) the splitkv module builds at import and self-checks in prepare(), which adds compile time against the 15-minute budget but is already paid on master. It also explains why full decode_16/32 sit at ~330/490 us in the base now; do not mistake that for a movement of this run.

stack-align-par-sidestream-sliding1 (8fa8fbf): shares code with this change, not shapes. It brought in the helpers (_counters, _inv_freq, _sliding_fused_kernel) and master's batch-1 _sliding_forward. _counters is keyed by (batch, hkv), so the B=16 and B=1 ticket buffers are separate. Its T>32 align/side-stream work never runs at T=16. The patch's first hunk would re-define all of these helpers; Python would keep the later, identical copy, so behaviour is unchanged, but the file is messier and a later stack could break. Reuse master's copies instead.

small-t-launch-minimal-dense-chain-pdl (f1f2f35): T<=32 PDL chain that starts after attn_boundary/o GEMM. The fused Triton kernel issues no griddepcontrol, but neither does master's FA3/FusedRMSNormGate before the cuBLAS o GEMM, so the PDL edge is unchanged. Both stacks that showed +5.2-5.5% were built on this base, so the interaction has already been measured and is not a confound.

fa3-hdim128-head-pairing-batched, marlin-block-m-cap-16, post-expert-norm-triton-small-t, sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8: disjoint (full-layer FA3 or downstream MoE/router), and the o GEMM operand is still [T,1024] bf16 in the same layout. No confound.
interference: No companion is warranted. The gate reads config only (window != 0, q_len 1, page 1, 2 <= batch <= 16). Only sliding decode_16 changes kernels, and the run itself carries 11 untouched shapes as noise controls, so a gain or a loss there belongs to the fused path. No landed hypothesis shares the replaced kernels, so an ab-revert would measure the same thing. A splits control (S=4 via _num_splits vs S=16) would isolate a sub-choice, but only if the implementer keeps S=16 as specified. Pin it in the build instead of spending a check on it. Relation to sliding-cluster-c4-decode32-port: the bands are disjoint and both attribute. This hypothesis covers sliding/q_len 1/page 1/batch 2..16 (scored: decode_16); the cluster port covers 17..32 (scored: decode_32); batch 1 stays on master's _sliding_forward. Each run's target shape is a byte-identical control in the other run, so the two results do not mix. One caution for the pair: decode_32 was not left on FA3 because Triton had nothing to offer there. This same Triton path gained +3.1%, +4.1% and +4.8% (paired) at sliding decode_32 in b01fd2df, 2193fc0d and b94e7973. The cluster port's own incumbent is FA3, so its decode_32 result attributes cleanly as cluster vs FA3. But its expected 242 -> ~226 (-6%) only beats the Triton alternative by ~1-3% per shape, which is under 2 sigma. The decision about who owns decode_32 therefore needs either the cluster port's prepare-time selector to also time the Triton S=16 path at B=32 (preferred: free, no check spent), or, if the cluster port lands, a later band-widen check of this path to 2..32 run against the cluster path. That is a follow-up for the cluster hypothesis, not a companion here. To keep both ports stackable without a textual fight, structure kernel_fn's sliding dispatch as an if/elif chain on config: batch==1 -> _sliding_forward; 2<=batch<=16 -> this path; (cluster later adds 17<=batch<=32); else master. Both hypotheses then touch adjacent elif lines.
rules_flags: None blocking. The path is the same code as the three earlier runs, which passed 13/13 and the timed checks: config-only gate; torch.empty workspaces sized from shapes; _counters zeroed once eagerly and reset in-kernel (hold no data); _SLIDING_FUSED_ON/try-except keyed on config only; queries kept bf16 (finer than the FP8 floor); KV stored FP8 E4M3; window covers all 2048 keys across the 16 splits; no host sync in kernel_fn.

Keep the patch's try/except fallback, and make its key include page_size (the patch's fkey already does). A launch exception during graph capture should not occur because the first call is eager, but the fallback must branch on the config key only, never on tensor values.

Do not add a second definition of _INV_FREQ/_COUNTERS/_counters/_sliding_fused_kernel: re-defining a dict at import would reset caches used by the batch-1 path. It is harmless at import time, but it is a rules-adjacent 'state reset' smell for the checker and reviewers.
open_questions: Change text should say explicitly: splits = 16 at q_len 1 (as the patch's _sliding_forward_batched), NOT _num_splits(batch, hkv) (= 4 at B=16), and reuse master's helpers rather than applying the patch's first hunk. Otherwise the run measures an untested S=4 configuration.

Correct the gate description: with page == 1, the batch-8 test (page 64) runs FA3 and only the batch-9 test exercises this path. Either accept that or drop the page==1 term (the kernel handles PAGE as a constexpr and passed the page-64 batch-8 test in all three earlier runs). Dropping it would add test coverage and does not touch the cluster port's band, which is gated by batch.

Read the fused kernel's own time on sliding decode_16 from the profile (_sliding_fused_kernel row) against master's FA3 main + combine + glue, so the per-kernel saving is recorded, not just the shape delta.

stack-align-par-sliding-batched (b94e7973) failed on full verify_1 (rc 112, 13/13 tests) on a shape neither of its parents gates, and master (which carries align-par) has since passed. Treat it as unrelated unless the full verify_1 failure reappears here.
For the cluster port: make its prepare-time selector time the Triton S=16 path at B=32 alongside FA3 and the cluster kernel, so the decode_32 band owner is chosen on measured kernel time.
